milestones.title: Kolachi founded
milestones.detail: Merchants from the silted-up port of Kharak Bandar built a new fortified settlement, defended with cannon brought from Muscat, beside a pool called Kolachi-jo-Kun at the head of the harbour.
milestones.source: Imperial Gazetteer of India (1908), vol. 15, 'Karachi City', pp. 11-17, https://archive.org/details/imperialgazettee15grea; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karachi

milestones.title: Talpurs take Karachi
milestones.detail: After three Baloch expeditions the Talpur rulers of Sindh took the town from the Khan of Kalat. They built a fort at Manora in 1797 to protect the harbour.
milestones.source: Imperial Gazetteer of India (1908), vol. 15, 'Karachi City', pp. 11-17, https://archive.org/details/imperialgazettee15grea; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manora_Fort,_Karachi

milestones.title: British capture Karachi
milestones.detail: HMS Wellesley bombarded Manora Fort on 3 February 1839 and East India Company troops occupied the town, then confined to the walled quarter with about 8,000 to 14,000 people.

milestones.title: Sindh annexed; Karachi its administrative centre
milestones.detail: With Napier's conquest and annexation of Sindh, Karachi passed formally into British possession and the province's capital was moved there from Hyderabad.
milestones.source: Imperial Gazetteer of India (1908), vol. 15, 'Karachi City', pp. 11-17, https://archive.org/details/imperialgazettee15grea

milestones.title: Napier Mole completed
milestones.detail: The causeway linking the town with the island of Kiamari was completed under Commissioner Bartle Frere, opening the harbour to larger ships.
milestones.source: Imperial Gazetteer of India (1908), vol. 15, 'Karachi City', pp. 11-17, https://archive.org/details/imperialgazettee15grea

milestones.title: Railway to Kotri opens
milestones.detail: The Scinde Railway began operating between Karachi and Kotri on the Indus.
milestones.source: Aitken, Gazetteer of the Province of Sind (1907), via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Karachi

milestones.title: Manora breakwater completed
milestones.detail: The 1,503 ft breakwater, begun in 1869, sheltered the entrance channel and allowed the bar to be deepened.
milestones.source: Imperial Gazetteer of India (1908), vol. 15, 'Karachi City', pp. 11-17, https://archive.org/details/imperialgazettee15grea

milestones.title: Linked to the Indian railway network
milestones.detail: Karachi was connected with the rest of British India's railway system; by 1899 it was the largest wheat-exporting port in the East.
milestones.source: Heitzman (2008), The City in South Asia, https://archive.org/details/cityinsouthasia0000heit, via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karachi

milestones.title: Tramway begins operating
milestones.detail: A tramway began operating; by the 1900s the East India Tramway ran along the Napier Mole between Kiamari and the town.
milestones.source: Baillie (1890), Kurrachee: Past, Present and Future, via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Karachi; Imperial Gazetteer of India (1908), vol. 15, 'Karachi City', pp. 11-17, https://archive.org/details/imperialgazettee15grea

milestones.title: Plague reaches Karachi
milestones.detail: The first case occurred in the old town in December 1896; nearly 3,400 people died in the first year and 19,010 by March 1904.
milestones.source: Imperial Gazetteer of India (1908), vol. 15, 'Karachi City', pp. 11-17, https://archive.org/details/imperialgazettee15grea

milestones.title: Capital of the new province of Sindh
milestones.detail: Sindh was separated from the Bombay Presidency on 1 April 1936 with Karachi as its capital.

milestones.title: Capital of Pakistan
milestones.detail: Karachi became the national capital at independence. About 470,000 refugees from India had arrived by May 1948, and the population tripled between 1941 and 1951.
milestones.source: Zamindar (2010), The Long Partition and the Making of Modern South Asia; Gayer (2014), Karachi: Ordered Disorder and the Struggle for the City, via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karachi

milestones.title: Federal capital moves to Rawalpindi
milestones.detail: The national capital was relocated from Karachi to Rawalpindi.

milestones.title: Karachi Circular Railway begins operating
milestones.detail: The Karachi Circular Railway, a suburban rail loop, began operating.

milestones.title: Green Line bus rapid transit in full operation
milestones.detail: The 26 km Green Line of the Karachi Breeze network, built between 2016 and December 2021, was reported fully operational in January 2022.

notes: Start date: 1729 is the usual date for the fortified settlement of Kolachi, from which Karachi grew. The 1908 Imperial Gazetteer says no town existed on the site before 1725. Older references are not to a town: a hamlet of 20-25 fishing huts (Dibro) stood by the harbour, an Ottoman admiral mentioned a small port called Kaurashi in 1553-54, and attempts to identify the harbour with Alexander's Krokola or with Debal are conjecture. The story that the village was named after Mai Kolachi is tradition. Population: nothing is available before 1838, so the first century of the settlement has no figure. 1838 and 1856 are contemporary estimates; 1872-1911 are censuses of the municipality and cantonment; 1921 and 1941 are census figures available only rounded, and no 1931 figure on the same definition was found. Wikipedia's demographic table (from a former city-government web page) gives higher figures from 1901 onward (136,297 in 1901, 435,887 in 1941), apparently for a wider area; it is not used. Landmarks: British-era heights come from the 1919 Sind Gazetteer. Left out: Manora Fort (1797), Mohatta Palace, the Karachi Port Trust and Municipal Corporation buildings and St Patrick's Cathedral (no height found); Holy Trinity Cathedral (1855), whose tower was 150 ft until its top two storeys were removed in 1904 and whose present height was not found; and Bahria Icon Tower (273 m), which CTBUH lists as on hold rather than completed. Habib Bank Plaza's completion year differs between CTBUH (1963) and the bank (1971); Empress Market's between Wikipedia (1889) and the 1919 gazetteer (opened 1891).
